headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill aims to shift the costs of grid infrastructure and capacity for large energy users, such as data centers, directly to those users rather than residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, ratepayer advocates, Governor Abigail Spanberger (with amendments).
news_headline: Virginia Legislature Bucks Governor's Amendments to Dominion-Backed Bill
news_summary: This article discusses how the Virginia legislature rejected some of Governor Spanberger's cost-saving suggestions for a bill, HB 1393, that would assign certain electric grid upgrade costs to data centers. The legislation aims to shift costs to high-load users to save residential electricity customers money and expand a power line burial program.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires local water authorities to report the total volume of water, including reclaimed water, provided to data centers, increasing transparency on their water consumption.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservationists, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
opponents: Data center industry (due to increased scrutiny and reporting burden).
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, championed by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, mandates local water authorities to report data center water usage, making these figures publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This initiative aims to address concerns about the significant water consumption of the rapidly growing data center industry.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities, requiring site assessments for sound profiles near residential areas and schools, and allowing localities to assess other environmental impacts.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, Del. Joshua E. Thomas, Sen. Danica A. Roem.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry (due to additional regulatory burdens).
news_headline: A Roanoke Delegate Helped Write Virginia's New Data Center Law. Here's What It Does, and What It Doesn't
news_summary: This article explains that Virginia's new law, HB 153, which took effect July 1, 2026, requires developers of large data centers to conduct site assessments for noise impacts on nearby residential areas and schools. While it mandates studies and disclosures, the law does not set specific noise limits, water caps, or setbacks, leaving some discretion to local officials.
